question.leadin: Give the following about the Crusades.
question.text: The Fourth Crusade, in the early 1200s, ended with the crusaders deciding to sack this Christian city, the capital of the Byzantine Empire, because they had lost their original source of funding.
question.clue: A bronze column originally from Delphi which depicted three entwined serpents holding up a golden bowl was relocated to this city's Hippodrome.

swap.leadin: Procopius wrote a lively, if historically and logically dubious, account of this man's reign.
swap.text: Name this Byzantine emperor and husband of Theodora who sought to reconquer the Western Roman Empire. He also constructed the Hagia Sophia.
swap.clue: A work denouncing this ruler becoming wealthy off of the "sky tax" includes the hyperbole that "ten thousand times ten thousand times ten thousand" people died during his reign.

question.leadin: Fans of two chariot racing teams, the Blues and the Greens, rioted in support of two condemned murderers in this event.
question.text: Name this 532 CE riot, which burned nearly half of the capital of the Eastern Roman Empire.
question.clue: Participants in this event wanted to crown Hypatius, but were outmaneuvered by the eunuch Narses and slaughtered by Mundus.

swap.text: This legal code passed by Justinian is sometimes named after him, and is composed of three main parts with a minor fourth section. The Codex and Digest are two of those sections.
swap.clue: For centuries, scholars puzzled over how three million lines were reduced to 150,000 during this work's creation.

question.text: This man, one of Justinian's generals, helped Narses ease the Nika Riots. He also led various wars against the Vandals and Ostrogoths and was given the last ever Roman Triumph at their conclusion.
question.clue: This general's campaigns informed Procopius's History of the Wars.

swap.text: This general of Justinian, who exiled Pope Silverius, reconquered much of the Western Roman Empire from the Vandals and Goths.
swap.clue: Early in this leader's career, together with Mundus they were instrumental in ensuring Hypatius and Pompeius did not take the throne.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the Byzantine Empire.
question.text: This Byzantine emperor lost the Battle of the Gates of Trajan to Tsar Samuel. However, this ruler got his revenge at the Battle of Kleidion where he gained his most notorious nickname after blinding prisoners.
question.answerHtml: Basil II [accept Basil the Bulgar Slayer or Basil Porphyrogenitus; Prompt on “Basil”]
question.clue: John Geometres wrote of how the "arrows of the Moesians broke the spears of the Avzonians" in describing this ruler's loss at the Battle of the Gates of Trajan.

swap.leadin: This former brothel-worker convinced her husband not to flee during the Nika Riots.
swap.text: Name this empress depicted in a mosaic with her husband in the Basilica of San Vitale in Ravenna.
swap.clue: A ruler with this name, who as a child acted in a portrayal of Leda and the Swan, was called the "most depraved" in the Anecdota.

question.text: Funded by Venice, this crusade looted Constantinople in 1204 and gave up on reaching the Middle East.
question.clue: In order to obtain the support of one city state, the participants of this event agreed to sack the city of Zara in Hungary.

swap.leadin: The Triumph of Orthodoxy engineered by Theodora largely ended support for this position.
swap.text: Identify this stance once popular in the Byzantine Empire wherein many "graven images" were removed from Orthodox churches.
swap.clue: This practice was carried out by mobs during the Dissolution of the Monasteries and again by the Puritans.

question.leadin: The Assyrian monk Alopen was a follower of this leader and brought his ideas to the Tang dynasty as the first known Christian missionary to China.
question.text: Name this fourth century Archbishop of Constantinople who taught that Christ had two distinct natures, human and divine. During the second half of the fifth century, a church named for this man flourished in Syria.
question.clue: This Patriarch of Constantinople was condemned by the Council of Ephesus for rejecting the title "Mother of God" for the Virgin Mary and teaching the existence of human and divine natures in Christ.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about innovations created by the Mongols.
swap.text: After founding the Mongol Empire, Genghis Khan created one of these systems, known as the Yassa, in order to maintain order. One of these systems created by Hammurabi of Babylon was carved into a stone stele.
swap.answerHtml: law codes [accept reasonable equivalents, such as legal systems; prompt on laws or codes]
swap.clue: One work of this kind included sections like the Digest and the Institutes.

question.leadin: This event was preceded by the escape of one prisoner each from the Blue and Green factions, who took shelter in a sanctuary as the public clamored for their release.
question.text: Name this event which occurred in January 532, in which protesters set fire to the Constantinople Hippodrome but were cornered and defeated by Belisarius and Mundus.

swap.text: This elite group of Norse fighters in the Byzantine army was formed when Basil the Bulgar-Slayer had his sister Anna married off to Vladimir the Great in exchange for their service.
swap.clue: As punishment for replacing this group with loyal Scythians, Michael V ("the fifth") was castrated and blinded by Harald Hardrada.

question.leadin: A cadet branch of this dynasty ruled the Italian duchy of Montferrat.
question.text: Identify this house whose members included Manuel II, who was controversially quoted by the Pope in 2006, and Michael VIII, who ascended to the throne after expelling the Latin Empire from Constantinople.

swap.text: Before becoming emperor, Constantine ruled this despotate that encompassed much of the Peloponnese peninsula whose capital was Mystras.
swap.clue: At that time, the entire Peloponnese was under the control of this Despotate, which had been established circa 1349 by Byzantine emperor John VI Cantacuzenus, and then taken over by the Palaeologus dynasty. It was ruled from a site near ancient Sparta.

question.text: This twelfth-century Byzantine princess became one of the first known women historians by penning the Alexiad, which narrates the dynasty-establishing reign of her father Alexios I.
question.answerHtml: Anna Comnena [or Anna Komnene; or Anna Comnenos; prompt on just her first or last name]
question.clue: This woman may have been inspired by the material laid out by her husband Nikephoros Bryennios the Younger to write a chronicle of her father's rule named the Alexiad.

swap.text: This dynasty's founder wedded his daughter into the noble family of Trebizond; that founder was Michael VIII. Its last ruler, Constantine XI, died in the Ottomans' siege of Constantinople.
swap.clue: The death of Constantine XI during the battle brought an end to the two hundred year rule of this final dynasty of Byzantine emperors.

question.leadin: This ruler, who introduced jousting and other Western European traditions to his kingdom, was hailed as a chivalric model by contemporaries, such as his chronicler John Kinnamos.
question.text: Identify this grandson of Alexius I, a Byzantine emperor who attempted an alliance with the papacy under Adrian IV. His attempt to regain Anatolia was halted at the Battle of Myriokephalon.
question.clue: While this ruler's armies besieged the island of Corfu, the Venetians mocked this ruler by having an African slave impersonate him.

swap.leadin: This clash took place near modern-day Konya, and the victory of the winning side is generally attributed to their ability to occupy the elevated position.
swap.text: Identify this 1176 battle in which the forces of the Sultanate of Rum, led by Arslan II, inflicted an overwhelming defeat on the Byzantine army.
